headline: Denser-Than-Water Liquid Transforms Energy Storage on Shallow Hills
meta_description: A 500 kW demonstrator uses liquid 2.5 times denser than water to enable pumped hydro storage on low-elevation terrain previously unsuitable for the technology.
summary_short: A new energy storage project harnesses a super-dense liquid to make pumped hydro viable on shallow terrain, opening possibilities for regions without tall hills.
body:
An energy storage project has successfully demonstrated a way to store electricity using a liquid 2.5 times denser than water—enabling pumped hydro systems to operate on much lower hills than conventional installations require.

The 500 kW demonstrator represents a significant shift in how energy storage might work across diverse landscapes. Traditional pumped hydro relies on elevation differences to store energy by pumping water uphill, then releasing it to generate power. This approach works brilliantly in mountainous regions but has limited options in flatter terrain.

By using a much denser liquid, the system achieves similar storage capacity with far less vertical distance needed. This opens possibilities for energy storage in regions previously excluded by geography, making renewable energy integration more feasible across a wider range of locations.

Works on much lower hills than normal pumped hydro
